pool.question: In simplified terms, how do diffusion-style image models generate an image?
options: They draw vectors from a template library
They search the internet for a matching photo
They start from random noise and remove it step by step, guided by the prompt
They copy one training image exactly
pool.explanation: Diffusion models iteratively denoise from random noise; they do not retrieve or copy images by design.

pool.question: A generated image of a real landmark includes architectural details that do not exist. Why?
options: Models learn visual patterns, not verified facts, so details can be inaccurate
pool.explanation: Models approximate patterns and can invent details; accuracy must be checked.

pool.question: Which criteria should you evaluate before adopting an image tool for client work? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Whether uploads and prompts are used for training
pool.explanation: Terms, data policy and features affect legality, confidentiality and workflow. Branding of the tool is irrelevant.

pool.question: A real-estate agency asks for AI images showing an apartment 'at its best', with a sea view it does not have. What should you advise?
options: Decline the misleading element; use real photos, with AI only for honest edits such as removing clutter if permitted and not misrepresentative
Use the images only on social media
Add a tiny 'AI' label and proceed
Create the images; buyers expect enhancement
pool.explanation: Depicting features that do not exist misleads consumers; labels do not cure misrepresentation.

pool.question: Which use is generally well suited to AI image generation?
options: News photographs of a real event
Before/after results for a diet product
pool.explanation: Ideation is a strong, low-risk use; the others risk deception.

pool.question: An agency wants to upload a client's customer photos to a free public generator to create stylized portraits. Which concerns apply? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Personal data and consent under data-protection laws
The portraits will automatically be copyrighted by the agency
The tool may make generations public or use uploads for training
pool.explanation: Data protection, tool data policies and confidentiality all apply. Automatic copyright is not guaranteed and is not a concern that justifies the upload.

pool.question: What is the most useful measure when comparing the cost of two image tools?
options: Cost per usable, approved image including iteration
pool.explanation: Iteration discards outputs; cost per usable image reflects real cost.

pool.question: Which element is missing from this prompt: 'Photo of a ceramic mug on a wooden table, soft morning light, warm tones'?
options: Composition/aspect ratio and space for text
pool.explanation: Subject, lighting, palette and medium are present; composition, framing and ratio are not.

pool.question: A campaign needs a consistent look across 20 images. Which approach is best?
options: Use a different tool per image
Write a new style description for each image
Use a documented style spec plus approved hero images as style references
Name a famous living artist in each prompt
pool.explanation: A reusable style spec and references create consistency responsibly.

pool.question: A client asks you to prompt 'in the style of' a specific living illustrator for a paid campaign. What is the best professional response?
options: Upload the illustrator's portfolio as references
Proceed because style is never protected
Explain the ethical, legal and reputational risks and propose describing visual characteristics or commissioning the illustrator
pool.explanation: Imitating a living artist raises ethical and potential legal issues; describing characteristics or commissioning is safer.

pool.question: When should you use subtle variations or fixed seeds?
options: During refinement, when you want controlled changes
pool.explanation: Subtle variations and fixed seeds help fine-tune; strong variations suit exploration.

pool.question: Which items belong in a prompt log entry? (Choose all that apply.)
pool.explanation: Logs document how an image was made; financial data does not belong there.

pool.question: Why add 'no text, no logos' to many prompts?
options: To reduce unwanted artifacts like garbled text or pseudo-logos
pool.explanation: Constraints reduce artifacts; they do not affect resolution, copyright status or platform rules.

pool.question: After 40 generations, a model still cannot produce an exact product label with correct small text. What should you do?
options: Switch approach: generate the scene and add the real label or text in a design tool
pool.explanation: A stop rule and approach switch save time and ensure accuracy.

pool.question: What does outpainting do?
options: Extends the image beyond its original edges
pool.explanation: Outpainting generates new content outside the original canvas.

pool.question: An inpainted patch looks smoother than the surrounding grainy photo. What should you do?
options: Match grain/noise and sharpness so the patch blends
pool.explanation: Texture mismatch reveals edits; matching grain blends the patch.

pool.question: A beauty brand wants AI to slim a model's waist and smooth skin heavily in a product ad. Which concerns apply? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Potential breach of advertising rules on misleading retouching in beauty ads
The image may become too large to upload
The model's consent to material changes to her appearance
Possible platform disclosure requirements for materially altered realistic content
pool.explanation: Misleading retouching, consent and disclosure are real issues; file size is not the concern.

pool.question: When is an AI upscaler's high 'creativity' setting most appropriate?
pool.explanation: Invented detail is harmless in abstract textures but alters identities and product details.

pool.question: Where should final headline text for an AI-illustrated ad usually be created?
options: In a design tool using brand fonts
pool.explanation: Design tools give accurate, on-brand typography in the correct fonts; generated text can be misspelled or garbled, and screenshots or no text do not meet the brief.

pool.question: You composite a real product photo into an AI scene, but it looks fake. Which checks address the problem? (Choose all that apply.)
pool.explanation: Lighting, color and perspective consistency make composites believable; file names do not.

pool.question: What is C2PA-based Content Credentials metadata used for?
options: Recording provenance, including AI generation or editing
pool.explanation: Content Credentials record provenance and can support platform labeling.

pool.question: Why is consistency across a campaign hard with image models?
options: Each generation starts from new random noise, so details drift
pool.explanation: Randomness causes drift unless anchored with references, seeds or fine-tuning.

pool.question: Which assets belong in a character bible? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Reference images of poses and expressions
pool.explanation: Descriptions, references and rules define the character; pricing is irrelevant.

That the photos are high resolution
Nothing if the ambassador is paid
pool.explanation: Likeness, image rights and policies must be addressed explicitly; payment for other work does not automatically cover synthetic use.

pool.question: What should you do after a model update changes your campaign's look?
options: Run a benchmark set, compare with approved references, adjust and log
pool.explanation: A benchmark set compared against approved references reveals style drift so you can adjust snippets or reference strength and log the change; ignoring it or abandoning AI are not proportionate responses.

pool.question: What is a do/don't gallery?
options: A visual set of approved and rejected outputs with reasons
pool.explanation: It aligns teams visually on what is on-brand.

pool.question: A client asks for 50 ad variations in one day. Which approach keeps quality and learning intact?

Randomly vary everything to maximize novelty
pool.explanation: Controlled, traceable variations with QA deliver usable test data and compliant creative.

pool.question: Which statement about using synthetic 'people' in marketing is correct?
options: They can be presented as real customers
They are always legally required to be labeled in every country
Avoid presenting synthetic people as real customers, employees or reviewers
pool.explanation: Presenting synthetic people as real endorsers is deceptive; labeling rules vary by jurisdiction and platform.

pool.question: A client wants to register a purely AI-generated mascot as the core of their brand and stop competitors copying it. What is the best advice?
options: Have a human illustrator create or substantially redraw the final mascot, document the process, run searches and assign rights
pool.explanation: Human authorship strengthens protection in many jurisdictions; searches and assignment manage risk.

pool.question: Which three questions should you separate when assessing AI image rights?
options: Is it protected, could it infringe, and what do the tool's terms allow
pool.explanation: Protection, infringement and terms are distinct legal questions.

pool.question: Which statements about copyright in AI images are accurate? (Choose all that apply.)
options: In the US, human selection, arrangement or modification of AI material can be protectable
UK law has a 'computer-generated works' provision whose application to generative AI is debated
Positions differ between countries and are evolving
Terms of service can create copyright where the law does not
pool.explanation: Terms allocate rights between parties but cannot create copyright the law does not recognize.

pool.question: Which content requires the strongest caution and likely consent or legal review?
options: A generic object on a table
A realistic image of a named public figure endorsing a product
pool.explanation: Real people and implied endorsement are high risk.

pool.question: A travel creator's sponsored post uses a realistic AI sunset over a destination. Which actions are appropriate? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Removing Content Credentials to keep the image 'clean'
Platform AI label and caption note
Real photos of the destination alongside to avoid misleading followers
pool.explanation: Both disclosures plus real imagery maintain honesty; stripping provenance undermines transparency.

pool.question: When do the EU AI Act's transparency obligations for deepfakes apply from?
pool.explanation: The AI Act's transparency obligations, including deepfake disclosure, apply from August 2026.

pool.question: An AI background accidentally contains a shape resembling a famous sportswear logo. What should you do?
options: Remove or alter it via editing before publication
pool.explanation: Pseudo-logos can imply affiliation or infringe; remove them.

pool.question: Which collaboration model uses AI mainly for ideation, with humans creating final assets?
pool.explanation: In the sketchbook model AI is used only for ideation and moodboards, while final assets are photographed, illustrated or designed by people.

pool.question: Which topics should AI-related contract terms address? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Ownership and limits of copyright in AI elements
Permitted AI use and tool/data restrictions
pool.explanation: Agreeing permitted use, ownership limits and who handles disclosure prevents disputes later; the designer's personal prompts are not a contractual matter.

pool.question: A studio's AI efficiency halves production time. It bills hourly and revenue drops. What is the most sustainable change?
options: Hide AI use and bill the old hours
Move to value-, package- or usage-based pricing while being transparent about process
pool.explanation: Pricing on outcomes captures value honestly; misrepresenting hours is dishonest.

pool.question: Which approach best addresses bias across an AI-illustrated campaign?
options: Check each image in isolation only
Review the campaign as a whole with an inclusion checklist and community input
pool.explanation: Reviewing the whole campaign with a checklist and community input catches patterns of stereotyping that single-image checks and tool filters miss.

pool.question: What should accompany published AI images for accessibility?
pool.explanation: Alt text makes images accessible to screen-reader users.

pool.question: A client insists on generating realistic 'customer' images for a testimonial carousel, saying 'everyone does it'. What is the best response?
options: Explain the deception and advertising-law risk, decline, and offer real customers with consent or clearly illustrative non-testimonial content
Use stock photos of models as customers
Comply but label in tiny text
pool.explanation: Fabricated testimonials mislead consumers and breach advertising rules whatever the label size; real customers with consent or clearly illustrative content keep the campaign honest.

pool.question: What should be reinvested when AI saves production time?
options: Better concepts, QA, accessibility and testing
pool.explanation: Time savings are best used to raise quality and learning.

pool.question: A client says: 'I wrote a 300-word prompt, so I'm the author of this generated image under US law.' Based on the US Copyright Office's January 2025 report on copyrightability, what is the best response?
options: Correct — any prompt over 100 words creates authorship
Prompts alone did not give enough control to make the user the author; protection needs human expressive contribution such as perceptible human work or creative selection, arrangement or modification
AI images can never contain any protectable material under any circumstances
Authorship belongs to the AI tool provider
pool.explanation: The Office concluded prompts alone were insufficient with then-current technology, but human expressive contributions (perceptible human work, creative selection/arrangement, modification) can be protected. It did not say AI-assisted works can never be protected, and length of prompt is not the test.

pool.question: What happened when the Thaler v. Perlmutter case reached the US Supreme Court in March 2026?
options: The Court ruled that AI systems can be authors
The Court declined to hear the case, leaving the lower court's human-authorship ruling in place
The Court ordered the Copyright Office to register all AI images
The Court sent the case back for a new trial on damages
pool.explanation: The Supreme Court denied certiorari on March 2, 2026, so the D.C. Circuit's decision requiring human authorship stands. It made no new ruling that AI can be an author.

pool.question: Your team relies on Content Credentials to trigger platform AI labels automatically. Which statements are accurate? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Screenshots and some exports or uploads can strip provenance metadata, so labels may not appear
Content Credentials record history such as tool and edits, but do not prove an image is true
If an image has no Content Credentials, it is definitely not AI-generated
You should test uploads per platform and still use manual labels where disclosure is required
pool.explanation: Metadata can be stripped, credentials show provenance rather than truth, and platforms differ — so test and label manually when required. Absence of credentials proves nothing about how an image was made.

pool.question: A YouTuber uses a realistic AI-generated scene of a real city street flooding in a news-style video. What does YouTube's policy expect?
options: Nothing — AI use never needs disclosure on YouTube
Disclose it using the altered or synthetic content setting at upload, because it is realistic and could mislead
Only mention it in a pinned comment after a week
Disclosure is only needed for AI music
pool.explanation: YouTube requires creators to disclose realistic altered or synthetic content during upload; YouTube may add labels itself and apply penalties for consistent non-disclosure. Minor or clearly unrealistic edits don't require it.

pool.question: In Photoshop's Generative Fill, a designer switches from an Adobe Firefly model to a partner model from another lab for a client banner. What should they check first?
options: Nothing — all models in the menu share identical terms
Whether the partner model's usage and commercial terms suit the client work, and note which model made the edit
Whether the monitor is calibrated to CMYK
Whether the file is under 1 MB
pool.explanation: Partner models can carry different terms from Adobe's own models, so check terms for client work and log the model used. Calibration and file size are unrelated to this decision.

pool.question: Image 7 of a mascot series comes back with six stripes instead of the canonical five, but everything else is right. What is the best next step?
options: Add image 7 to the reference folder so future images learn from it
Fix the stripe with a small inpaint, check it against the consistency scorecard, and only then approve it
Change the character bible to allow six stripes
Regenerate the entire series from scratch
pool.explanation: Targeted fixes plus a scorecard keep the bible as the source of truth. Adding drifted images to references compounds errors; changing the bible to match a mistake erodes consistency; full regeneration wastes good work.

pool.question: Which alt text best describes an AI-generated recruitment image for a careers page?
options: Three colleagues of different ages reviewing a project plan on a laptop in a bright office; headline reads 'Join our team'
pool.explanation: Useful alt text states what the image is, the detail that matters for the message, and any text in the image. Labels like 'AI image' or file names convey nothing to screen-reader users.

pool.question: A designer has changed the prompt three times, and a perfume bottle's label keeps coming out wrong. According to the course's diagnosis approach, what should they do next?
options: Keep rewording the prompt until it works
Add more adjectives such as 'luxury' and 'premium'
Switch mode: attach the real product photo as a reference or composite the real bottle, and set label text in the layout
Increase the upscaler's creativity to sharpen the label
pool.explanation: When a defect survives three prompt changes, change mode — references, editing or compositing. Labels are hard fine detail, so the real product photo and live text are the reliable fix. Adjectives and higher upscaler creativity make invented detail more likely.
